match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the objective-versus-subjective register choices an argument makes; they all cover narrative or literary voice (diction, rhythm, point of view), so this point needs a new card.

draft.title: Blending subjective and objective voice
card: presents facts, figures and evidence in a neutral tone. It avoids personal feelings and sounds fair and informed.
gives the writer's own opinion or feelings. It uses first person (I, we), emotive words and judgements such as shameful or wonderful.
Writers of arguments move between the two. Objective voice can build trust in the facts. Subjective voice can move the reader to feel or agree.
For example, a writer states that most local pools open fewer than four days a week, then adds: "It is a disgrace." The first sentence is objective and the second is subjective.
draft.remember: Objective voice gives evidence in a neutral tone. Subjective voice gives opinion. Arguments often use both for effect.

a.q: Which sentence from a newspaper opinion piece is written in an objective voice?
opts: The council recorded 112 road accidents on Elm Street last year
Elm Street is a deadly trap that the council simply ignores
I am sick of watching drivers speed along Elm Street
Anyone who cares about children must fix Elm Street now
a.why: The first option states a recorded figure in a neutral tone. The others use emotive words, I, or a judgement about what people should do, so they are subjective.
a.clue: Look for the sentence with no feelings or opinion in it.

b.q: A writer opens an argument about school canteens with two sentences of statistics on student health, then writes: "I find this shameful." What is the most likely effect of this move?
opts: The evidence earns trust, then the opinion sways feelings
The opinion earns trust, then the evidence sways feelings
Both parts are objective, so the tone stays neutral
Both parts are subjective, so the writer sounds biased
b.why: The statistics are objective and make the writer seem informed. The sentence with I and shameful is subjective and pushes the reader to share the feeling. The reverse is wrong, because the opinion is not what builds trust in the facts.
b.clue: Decide which sentence is evidence and which is opinion, then think about what each does.
